title: Benefit-Period Day Numbering Across Episodes (Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage)
content:
**Rule.** For Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage, benefit days are counted per benefit period across every coverage episode of the resident, never per episode. The benefit period of an episode is the one on the Medicare eligibility response at admission: it began with the inpatient admission recorded as the benefit period start date and ends only after the resident has gone the benefit-period break of consecutive days without inpatient hospital or SNF care. The benefit-period day number of a covered day is the SNF days already used in the period before the episode, plus the net covered days booked earlier in the same episode, plus one; because the eligibility response already includes earlier episodes of the same period in the prior SNF days, those days are never added a second time. A day is booked only when its benefit-period day number does not exceed the benefit-period day limit. Days past the limit are not Part A days at all; they belong to whatever payer source covers the stay afterwards.

**Quantities.**

- *First benefit day of a block* — the prior SNF days in the period recorded on the episode, plus the net covered days booked earlier in the episode (booked days less reversed days), plus one.
- *Last benefit day of a block* — the first benefit day plus the block's day count, less one.

**Authority.** The prior SNF days in the period and the covered days already booked are read from the episode's system record.

*Hypothetical worked example:* an episode records 14 prior SNF days in the period; earlier in the episode 23 days were booked and 3 reversed. The next block's first benefit day is 14 plus 20 plus one, that is day 35; a block of 12 days runs from day 35 to day 46. Each of those days is booked only because its number does not exceed the benefit-period day limit.
